subject.title: [security] Proxmox redirects can disclose API tokens across origins

question: Should authenticated Proxmox API requests reject all redirects, or retain only redirects that exactly preserve the initiating scheme, canonical hostname, and effective port?
rationale: Either policy can be secure, but whether same-origin Proxmox redirects are a supported operational requirement is a maintainer-owned compatibility and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Preserve exact-origin redirects
options.body: Implement the documented scheme, canonical-hostname, and effective-port boundary for every hop and cover allowed same-origin redirects plus rejected cross-boundary cases.

options.title: Reject every redirect
options.body: Fail any redirect from authenticated Proxmox requests if maintainers do not need redirect compatibility for supported deployments.

recommendation.title: Preserve exact-origin redirects
recommendation.body: Implement the documented scheme, canonical-hostname, and effective-port boundary for every hop and cover allowed same-origin redirects plus rejected cross-boundary cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the concrete security analysis and can clarify the demonstrated boundary while a repository owner confirms the supported redirect contract.
